title: Jaldapara, Buxa and Jayanti on a budget
start: NJP railway station or Bagdogra airport
end: NJP railway station or Bagdogra airport

cost_split.item: Homestays and budget lodges, 5 nights with dinner and breakfast
Shared Jaldapara safari seat, forest fees and guide share

meta_description: 5 nights in the eastern Dooars on a budget: Jaldapara rhinos, the walk to Buxa Fort, Lepchakha and the Jayanti riverbed, from ₹11,000 per person.
summary: The eastern Dooars by train and shared car: two nights in Madarihat for Jaldapara's rhinos and Totopara, two nights up at Buxa Fort with a dawn at Lepchakha, and a last night on the Jayanti riverbed. Big wildlife, real history and good walking at shoestring cost.
intro: Alipurduar district holds three of the region's best experiences within an hour or two of each other: Jaldapara's rhino grassland, the forest walk to Buxa Fort, and the white riverbed of Jayanti under the Bhutan hills. This plan connects them by the Dooars line and shared cars, with homestays and budget lodges throughout.

It suits travellers who are happy to walk: the 5 km climb to Buxa is the heart of the trip, and you sleep two nights on the ridge to have time for Lepchakha. Jaldapara gives you one dawn jeep safari on a shared seat; add another if the budget allows.
highlights: Dawn jeep safari for Jaldapara's rhinos
The forest path to Buxa Fort
Sunrise from Lepchakha over the plains

days.title: Train from NJP to Madarihat
days.drive: ≈ 125 km · 4–5 h by train or bus
days.text: Take a morning Dooars line train from NJP or Siliguri Junction to Madarihat; check the current timetable. The line runs past tea gardens, the Teesta and the forest belt around Chapramari. Check into a budget lodge or homestay in Madarihat, walk to the forest counter to confirm your shared jeep seat for tomorrow, and buy snacks for the early start. Early dinner and bed.

days.title: Jaldapara at dawn, Totopara by afternoon
days.text: Board a shared jeep for the first safari slot around 6 am in winter, into the tall grass where rhinos graze in the open early. Back for breakfast. After lunch, share a car with other travellers to Totopara, about 22 km away, home of the Toto community and its endangered language. Walk the lanes quietly, have tea at a village shop and ask before photographing anyone. Back to Madarihat by dusk.

days.title: To Santalabari and up to Buxa
days.drive: ≈ 60 km by train or bus and shared car, then 5 km on foot
days.text: Take a morning train or bus east to Hasimara or Rajabhatkhawa, then a shared car to Santalabari, the road head. Pay forest fees and start the 5 km stone path through forest to Buxa, about two to three hours up. Check into a homestay in Buxa village by afternoon, walk to the fort ruins and the memorial to the revolutionaries detained here in the 1930s, and watch the light go over the plains.
days.spend: ₹100 train or bus + ₹250 car share + ₹150 fees + ₹150 lunch

days.title: Lepchakha sunrise, a slow Buxa day
days.text: Walk up to Lepchakha before dawn with a local guide and a torch, about an hour and a half, for sunrise over the Dooars plains and rivers. Tea in the village and back down to Buxa for breakfast. The rest of the day is free: rest, read, walk a short way along village paths, and talk with your homestay family, many of whom are Dukpa, about Buxa's past, including the Tibetan monks who lived here from 1959 to about 1971.

days.title: Down to Jayanti and its riverbed
days.drive: 5 km on foot, then ≈ 30 km by shared car
days.text: Walk down to Santalabari after breakfast and share a car to Jayanti via Rajabhatkhawa. Check into a river-facing homestay. In the late afternoon walk out onto the vast stony bed of the Jayanti river, cross a couple of shallow channels and watch the Bhutan hills turn blue and purple. Leave before dusk, when elephants may cross. Dinner with your hosts, who can tell you about the Mahakal cave and Pokhri lake.

days.title: Alipurduar and the train home
days.drive: ≈ 30 km by car, then ≈ 170 km by train
days.text: A last dawn walk along the riverbank for birds, then breakfast and a shared car or local bus to Alipurduar Junction, about an hour. Take a train back to NJP; services and timings vary, so check before you travel and book a reserved seat if possible. Arrive in NJP by evening.

Skip a second Jaldapara safari and use the free afternoon for Totopara or tea gardens instead.
Leave heavy luggage at a Madarihat lodge and come back for it, or carry only a daypack for the whole loop.

faqs.q: Is five nights enough for the eastern Dooars?
faqs.a: Yes, for Jaldapara, Buxa and Jayanti at a steady pace. Add a night at Jayanti if you want the full Mahakal cave walk, or a night at Chilapata for the Nalraja Garh ruins. Five nights is the minimum to avoid rushing the Buxa walk.

faqs.q: Can we do this trip without a car?
faqs.a: Yes. Dooars line trains reach Madarihat, Hasimara, Rajabhatkhawa and Alipurduar, and shared cars and local buses cover the gaps to Santalabari and Jayanti. Travel in the mornings, when services are most frequent, and ask homestay hosts for jeep timings.

faqs.q: How hard is the walk to Buxa?
faqs.a: About 5 km on a stone path with a steady climb to around 850 m, two to three hours up. It is easy to moderate and needs no trekking experience. Lepchakha above is steeper but short. Good shoes and water are enough.

Yes, it is a village anyone can visit, with no special permit for Indians. Go as a respectful guest: walk the lanes, buy tea and snacks locally, ask before photographing anyone, and do not treat residents as an attraction.

faqs.q: Can we see tigers in Buxa?
faqs.a: Almost certainly not. A tiger was camera-trapped in December 2021 after no records since 1998, and sightings remain extremely rare. Buxa is about the forest, the fort and the views; elephants, gaur and birds are the wildlife you will meet.

faqs.q: Where do we stay at Madarihat on a budget?
faqs.a: Small lodges and homestays along the highway and in nearby villages charge about ₹1,200–2,000 per person with meals. The WBTDC Jaldapara Tourist Lodge costs more. Book ahead for winter weekends, when Bengal families fill the town.

faqs.q: What if the train timings do not fit?
faqs.a: Use buses on the highway between Madarihat, Hasimara and Alipurduar, which run frequently by day, and shared or hired cars for short hops. A car from Madarihat to Santalabari costs about ₹2,000–2,800 and can be shared.

In the dry season, near the village and in daylight, yes. Cross only shallow channels and leave before dusk, when elephants may cross. After heavy rain upstream the water can rise suddenly; move to the bank at once if it changes.

faqs.q: When is the best time for this trip?
faqs.a: November to February is ideal: dry paths, clear Lepchakha sunrises and good rhino sightings. October and March are fine. April is hot on the plains. Avoid June to September, when parks close and paths are slippery.
